findings.description: `QodoApi.call` ignores the MCP tool result's `isError` flag and parses its text as a successful result. When a tool-level error contains JSON text, `review-wait` treats that error object as review data and can continue polling until timeout instead of reporting the API failure.

findings.description: `onPoll` reads only the pull request's issue-comment endpoint. Qodo comments attached to code lines are available through the separate pull-review-comment endpoint, so their text and edits never enter the saved comment snapshots.

citations.citation:
Qodo rewrites its review comment in place after every push, so the first version is lost if you wait. Poll every 20 seconds (up to 20 minutes) and save the raw comments as soon as "Code Review by Qodo" appears, and again after each new commit:

```bash
D=<evidence>/day-NN
gh api repos/<github>/issues/<pr>/comments > $D/<key>-pr<pr>-issue-comments.<commit>.raw.json
gh api repos/<github>/pulls/<pr>/comments  > $D/<key>-pr<pr>-review-comments.<commit>.raw.json

evidence.explanation: The new poller requests only issue comments; the repository's existing review procedure retrieves both issue and pull-review comments as separate evidence.

findings.title: Inline review comments are not saved

findings.description: `main` fetches one page of check runs for the correct head SHA and builds `ci` solely from that page's `check_runs` array. If the commit has additional pages, a failed check on one of them is absent from the saved CI result and console output.

evidence.explanation: The check-runs request has no pagination and its single returned array is the sole input to `ci`.

findings.title: The CI record can omit failed checks

findings.description: `pushedAt` is populated from the commit's `commit.committer.date`, which describes the commit rather than its arrival on GitHub. When a commit is pushed after it was created, the record attributes the intervening delay to Qodo's push-to-review-start time.

  const pushedAt = gh("api", `repos/${github}/commits/${headSha}`, "--jq", ".commit.committer.date").trim();

evidence.explanation: The GitHub query explicitly selects `commit.committer.date`, and that value is stored and printed as `pushedAt`.

findings.title: Recorded push times can predate the push

findings.description: `onPoll` calls the issue-comments endpoint once, without pagination, and searches only that response for Qodo timestamps. On a pull request whose Qodo comment falls beyond the first page, its versions are never detected or saved.

evidence.explanation: The new request omits pagination, although the existing GitHub API caller demonstrates the repository's `--paginate --slurp` pattern.

findings.title: Later-page review comments disappear

findings.description: `QodoApi.call` parses the tool text before `review-wait` can write it, and the script writes only the final parsed review after polling ends. If parsing fails or a later poll errors, the API output already received is not saved, so the failed review cannot be reconstructed from its evidence folder.

evidence.explanation: Both the JSON-RPC response and tool text are parsed in the client, while the only API file write occurs after `waitForReview` has returned.

findings.title: Failed reviews leave no raw API evidence

findings.description: `waitForReview` polls comments before fetching Qodo's review state and returns immediately when that fetch says `complete`. If Qodo edits a comment between those two calls, the command performs no final comment poll and saves the older snapshot.

evidence.explanation: The call order is comment poll, review fetch, immediate return on completion; the comment snapshot is written only by the poll callback.

findings.title: Final comment edits can go unsaved

+      : JSON.parse(

findings.description: `rpc` recognizes a JSON response only when its first character is `{`; otherwise it treats the body as server-sent events and parses only the last `data:` line. A valid JSON body with leading whitespace falls through to an empty object, while an event with multiple data lines loses all but the last line.

evidence.explanation: The parser dispatches using `startsWith("{")`, then selects only the final `data:` line; `call` depends on the resulting `json.result` for tool content.

findings.title: Valid API responses can lose their result
